explanation: Sandhi (सन्धि) literally means 'joining' or 'union'. It is the process by which sounds at the boundary of words or morphemes combine and change. Sandhi makes Sanskrit flow smoothly when spoken. There are three main types: vowel sandhi (स्वर सन्धि), consonant sandhi (व्यञ्जन सन्धि), and visarga sandhi (विसर्ग सन्धि).

types.name: Vowel Sandhi (स्वर सन्धि)
types.description: When two vowels meet at a word boundary, they combine or change. This is the most common type of sandhi for beginners.

types.name: Consonant Sandhi (व्यञ्जन सन्धि)
types.description: When a consonant at the end of a word meets another sound at the beginning of the next word, changes may occur.

rules.english_rule: Final t before a vowel becomes d

types.name: Visarga Sandhi (विसर्ग सन्धि)
types.description: The visarga (ः) at the end of a word can change when the next word starts with certain sounds.

rules.english_rule: aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes o

examples.breakdown: देव (god) + आलयः (house) → अ + आ = आ → देवालयः
हिम (snow) + आलयः (abode) → अ + आ = आ → हिमालयः
सूर्य (sun) + उदयः (rising) → अ + उ = ओ → सूर्योदयः
विद्या (knowledge) + आलयः (house) → आ + आ = आ → विद्यालयः
नर (man) + इन्द्रः (lord) → अ + इ = ए → नरेन्द्रः
महा (great) + ईश्वरः (lord) → आ + ई = ए → महेश्वरः
सत् (good/true) + जनः (person) → त् + ज = ज्ज → सज्जनः
